brief: Goldman's weekly client-flow roundup across ten themes. France's fiscal strain broadened into a wider European sovereign and rates story, tightening financial conditions enough to reduce the case for further ECB hikes even though higher oil and inflation keep another hike alive; GS argues fiscal, not monetary, action is the real fix. European banks sold off on leveraged-fund degrossing plus sovereign concerns, with sellers in ING, Intesa, StanChart and Lloyds; a 1% fall in bond fair-value marks implies roughly 15bp of average CET1 impact against a 14.1% sector CET1, hitting BCP, HSBC and STAN hardest. Pasquariello stays tactically bullish on equities on growth, earnings and flows, while GS Economics sees only a modest growth hit from higher rates that worsens if rates stay elevated. Prime book shows Mag7 near 22% of US exposure, the highest since 2022, and Semis near 12%, even as overall net positioning sits in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback. TMT earnings setup is selective, with tactical upside in AMAT, CDNS and MCHP against downside risk in QCOM, KLAC and WDC. Waller turned more hawkish on two further hikes, but GS still expects just one final December 25bp hike.
